executive_preview: The clearest industry signal this week is a widening split between EV ambition and execution. Automakers are moving forward with domestic battery production, U.S. EV assembly, vehicle-to-grid programs and faster-charging products, but multiple programs remain constrained by software, infrastructure, regulatory limits, financial pressure and delayed launches.

lead_development.title: Automotive retail is shifting toward distributed, digital and experience-led transactions
lead_development.what_happened: Hertz is closing its dedicated used-car stores while emphasizing HertzCarSales.com, Amazon Autos, eBay and TestDrive+ at more than 300 rental locations. Carvana is expanding same-day delivery in Massachusetts, while wholesale used-vehicle prices were described as steady in the CBT News weekly roundup.
lead_development.why_it_matters: The evidence points to fewer dedicated retail footprints and more use of existing vehicle networks, digital merchandising and extended test-drive formats. Traditional dealers may face greater competition from asset-light sellers, but the model also reinforces the value of physical access, vehicle condition transparency and convenient delivery.

signals.title: Domestic battery and EV production are moving from investment announcements into validation
signals.teaser: Ford began producing LFP battery cells at its Marshall, Michigan, facility and is shipping them for Fathom prototypes.

signals.title: EV product timing is becoming a strategic liability
signals.teaser: Scout Motors began validation builds but confirmed that Traveler and Terra customer deliveries will not begin until 2028, roughly two years later than earlier production expectations.

signals.title: Used-vehicle depreciation is increasingly disconnected from new-car pricing
signals.teaser: Edmunds data showed the average three-year-old vehicle selling for $16,562 below its original sticker price in Q3, the widest gap in its records.

downside.title: Software defects may increase recall frequency, service complexity and consumer skepticism toward EVs and connected vehicles.
downside.teaser: Recalls involving Acura braking, Ford Transit body controls and BMW high-voltage software occurred alongside reported Tesla driver-assistance crashes.

upside.title: Build retail strategies around affordable hybrids and entry-level EVs rather than relying exclusively on premium electrification.
upside.teaser: Hyundai is maintaining an affordable Elantra strategy, Toyota is expanding hybrids into pickups, Subaru is applying hybrid power to an off-road model, and Volkswagen reports strong demand for lower-priced EVs.
